key_insight: Adding 1 wt.% CeO2 or La2O3 to HVOF-sprayed WC–12Co reduced porosity, refined grains, and improved microhardness and wear performance without affecting bond strength.
engineering_relevance: Rare-earth oxide additions offer a route to denser, more wear-resistant WC–12Co coatings while preserving adhesion.
method: Deposit unreinforced and CeO2- or La2O3-reinforced WC–12Co coatings using HVOF.
Compare microstructure, phases, bond strength, microhardness, abrasive wear, and friction.
Examine worn surfaces using SEM to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: At 1 wt.% addition, CeO2 and La2O3 increased microhardness by 6% and 4%, respectively; La2O3 achieved the minimum wear rate of 3.5 × 10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), while CeO2 achieved the lowest friction coefficient of 0.4.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or statistical uncertainty for hardness and tribological results, limiting transfer to service conditions.
paper_title: EFFECT OF CEO2 AND LA2O3 REINFORCEMENTS ON MECHANICAL, TRIBOLOGICAL AND MICROSTRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF WC–12CO COATING BY HIGH-VELOCITY OXYGEN FUEL DEPOSITION TECHNIQUE
